context.description: The Riverland is the stretch of the Murray River from Loxton and Waikerie to the Victorian border, lined with citrus groves, vineyards and irrigated orchards. Renmark, Berri, Barmera and Loxton make good bases, each with its own museum, lake or riverfront. Between them lie floodplain parks, wetlands and red gum forests that are best explored by canoe. Paddle steamers and houseboats still work the river, and roadside giants like the Big Orange mark the fruit-growing towns.

context.description: Coober Pedy is an opal-mining town on the Stuart Highway in outback South Australia, where homes and churches are dug into the hillsides. Visitors tour old mines and underground dwellings, and the Serbian Orthodox church is bored out of solid rock. Outside town, the Kanku-Breakaways' eroded hills and the pale Moon Plain have both served as film locations. About 20 km out there is no electric light, so the night sky is easy to see.

context.description: Innamincka is a small township on Cooper Creek in South Australia's far north-east, home to about 15 permanent residents. The former Australian Inland Mission building is now the national parks visitor centre, with displays on the Yandruwandha and Yawarrawarrka Traditional Owners, pastoral settlement and the Burke and Wills expedition. Innamincka Regional Reserve covers more than 1.3 million hectares of creek waterholes and arid country. Malkumba-Coongie Lakes National Park, about 100 km north-west, is a Ramsar-listed wetland.

context.description: The Copper Coast is the northern Yorke Peninsula around Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta, where Cornish miners worked copper from the 1860s. Moonta Mines is a state heritage area with a museum, tourist railway and walking trails, and Kadina's Farm Shed Museum holds the stump-jump plough. Wallaroo has a heritage and nautical museum and North Beach, while Moonta Bay and Port Hughes add jetties and swimming beaches. A sealed rail trail links Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta.
